add.issue.name: GUI log panel: pane scrolled into empty space while a movie plays

edit.description.md:
Reported: with the log panel open and the theatre replaying a segment, the pane sits scrolled over an empty area and shows no lines.

Reproduce, find why the foot snap on `moment` does not hold during playback, fix, add a regression test.

add.issue.name: epiq skill: ask which name to take, self-assign session tickets, name the window

edit.description.md:
Three additions to .claude/skills/epiq/SKILL.md:

1. When other agent sessions may be running, do not pick a name silently: list the existing provider identities from `epiq_contributor_list` and ask the user which to assume.
2. Name the terminal window after the identity. The model cannot reach the tty from a session, so ask the user to rename the window (`/rename <name>` in Claude Code).
3. A ticket you file and will do in this session is assigned to yourself on creation. Picking up a ticket assigned to someone else is fine, but ask the user first.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #233, commit VYD2Q2J on branch VYD2Q2J-skill-names. Replaces the clash bullet with an ask-first rule (list the provider names from epiq_contributor_list, ask before epiq_actor_assume binds the process), adds a window-naming rule (the session has no tty, so the announcement asks the user to /rename), and a self-assign-on-file rule with ask-before-taking-others-tickets.

add.issue.comment.md: Reproduced. The one-node hover arrow is absolutely positioned inside the scroll pane at the hovered row's offsetTop, and an absolutely positioned child extends the pane's scrollable overflow even at opacity 0. Hover a row deep in a tall log, start a movie: the rows go, the arrow stays thousands of px down, and the foot snap scrolls into that empty overflow until the log grows back to it. Same thing on folding a day after hovering below the fold. Fix: park a stray arrow (one past the end of the column) at the top before either snap, so it holds no overflow open.
add.issue.comment.author: HVK8KMV924DBNFBDQV8RCZ9S06

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #235, commit VPR4FJ5 on branch VPR4FJ5-log-arrow-overflow. The hover arrow, absolutely positioned in the scroll pane, kept the pane's scrollable overflow open at the last hovered row's offset after the rows were gone, so the foot snap scrolled into empty space. EventLog now parks an arrow that sits past the end of the column back at the top before either snap (timeline move, or a line landing while pinned). Regression test in event-log.pw.ts: hover the last row of an overflowing log, start a movie, expect zero overflow on the emptied pane — 54 px without the fix.
